questions.question: Why do animals have specific adaptations, such as webbed feet or camouflage?
options: To make them look different from other species
To help them survive in their particular environment
To allow them to change their DNA during their lifetime
To prevent them from interacting with other species

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a behavioural adaptation in animals?
options: Having thick, insulating fur
Possessing sharp claws for catching prey
Being nocturnal to avoid daytime heat and predators
Having a streamlined body shape for swimming

questions.question: Why is maintaining a high level of biodiversity crucial for ecosystems?
options: It ensures that all habitats eventually become identical.
It is important for maintaining healthy and resilient habitats.
It prevents any evolutionary changes from occurring in species.
It reduces the total number of organisms that can live in an area.

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'gene pool' in biology?
options: The physical location where aquatic organisms reproduce
The total number of different species in a single ecosystem
The range of DNA and genetic variation within a species
A database storing the locations of endangered animals

questions.question: Which of these is a method used by scientists to help maintain and protect global biodiversity?
options: Introduction of invasive species to all habitats
Clearing natural forests for agricultural use
Using conservation, protection, and gene banks
Encouraging the overexploitation of natural resources

questions.question: Why do ecologists use sampling rather than counting every individual when estimating a population size?
options: It is impossible to count every single organism in an entire area.
Sampling is guaranteed to be 100% accurate without any estimation.
Counting individual organisms damages the habitat permanently.
Organisms cannot be identified if they are counted individually.

questions.question: What are quadrats, and what are they typically used to sample?
options: Large nets used to catch fast-flying birds and bats
Square frames used to sample plants or slow-moving animals
Traps designed to temporarily hold small nocturnal mammals
Chemical solutions used to extract organisms from soil samples

questions.question: Why is it important that quadrat sampling is usually done randomly?
options: To ensure that only the rarest species are counted
To make the fieldwork more physically challenging
To avoid bias in the results of the investigation
To guarantee that every single organism in the habitat is sampled

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a classification key in ecological studies?
options: To estimate the total biomass of a selected population
To help identify different species based on their characteristics
To measure changes in the temperature of a habitat
To map the boundaries of an endangered species' territory

questions.question: What components make up an ecosystem?
options: Only the physical, non-living parts of a habitat
Only the animal species that live in a particular area
A community of organisms interacting with each other and their non-living surroundings
A group of identical organisms that do not interact with other species

questions.question: Why are organisms in an ecosystem described as interdependent?
options: Because they depend upon each other for the resources they need to survive
Because they can survive completely independently of any other living thing
Because they all share the exact same genetic information
Because they only interact with non-living parts of their environment

questions.question: What vital role do decomposers play in sustaining life within an ecosystem?
options: They are the primary producers that generate energy from sunlight.
They break down dead organisms and recycle useful substances for reuse.
They actively hunt and control the population of top predators.
They prevent any energy from escaping the food chain.

questions.question: What does the term 'biodiversity' measure?
options: The total mass of all non-living matter in an ecosystem
The average life expectancy of animals in a habitat
The range of different living organisms present
The speed at which energy flows through a food chain

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical adaptation of a plant?
options: Growing towards a source of light
Having spines to deter consumers from eating it
Opening flowers only at specific times of day
Releasing seeds only when temperature rises

questions.question: What does a pyramid of biomass represent?
options: The total number of individual organisms at each stage of a food chain
The geographical distribution of different species in a habitat
The mass of living material in organisms at each stage of a food chain
The rate of reproduction of producers over a calendar year

questions.question: How is a pyramid of number constructed for a food chain?
options: By measuring the total dry mass of organisms at each level
By using the number of organisms at each trophic level
By counting only the number of different plant species present
By calculating the percentage of energy lost at each stage
